To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
epithelial cells do not adhere to, or spread upon, the free surfaces of epithelia, but that mesenchyme cells do.

the cells of an epithelial-mesenchymalmal system cannot attach to, or migrate upon, the free surfaces of other epithelia, and that the cells of such a system are capable of forming epithelial-bounding membrane.
the formation of epithelio- mesenchymal systems can be accounted for by the interactions between cells, and that a discontinuity in cell-cell contacts is necessary for the formation of epithelia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cellular interactions in the morphogenesis of epithelial-mesenchymalmal systems.
the role of cell-cell and cell-substratum interactions in the morphogenesis of epithelial mesenchymal systems.
the cellular interactions which determine the morphogenesis and organization of epithelial-mesenchymalmal systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contact interactions among cells are responsible for the organization of epithelial and mes-enchymal systems.
the formation of epithelia-bounding membranes is an intrinsic property of epithelium.
the formation of epithelio- mesenchymal systems is an expression of the cell contact interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of epithelia is an expression of the discontinuity between epithelial cells and their substratum, and the maintenance of the epithelial organization is an expression of their discontinuity from their mesenchymal neighbors.

epithelial and mesenohymal cells interact with each other and with noncellular substrata in a variety of ways, but that the interactions between epithelial cells are the most specific, and that these are responsible for the formation of the epithelial-bounding membrane.
(1) the formation of epithelio- mesenchymal systems can be accounted for, and (2) the formation of these systems is a consequence of the properties of the cells and not of their extracellular matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of epithelio-bounded membranes can be accounted in terms of the behavior of the cells, the interactions between the cells, and the interactions of the cells with their substratum.
the formation of an epithelial surface is an active process, and that the epithelial cells are the agents responsible for its formation.
the formation of epithelium is not a simple matter of cell aggregation.
